What games have the biggest inconsistency when it comes to the quality of level design?

There aren't many games I know where the level design work ethic fluctuates.

Do you have one in mind?

Dark Souls has beautiful places like anor londo, the painted world, and ash lake, as well as IMO won of the most atmospheric levels in gaming, the undead burg. The best part of dks level design is how all of the places connect together making it feel like a real world.

Then there is lost izalith, with it's infamous "lake of lava and animated dragonbutts copypasted across the landscape. The devs even admitted that they were forced to cut around a third of izalith because of publisher pressure to release the game.

Its such a jarring drop in polish from the rest of the game which has some of my favorite level design of any game.

Came here to mention this. Dark Souls is almost always a good answer for any question regarding game design, I've found!

So as a second choice I'll bring up the Mass Effect series. The level design is all over the place as a series and from game to game as well.

The devs even admitted that they were forced to cut around a third of izalith because of publisher pressure to release the game.

This happens so often in the industry that it's really kind of depressing. I've worked on more than a dozen console games and I'd say 10/12 of them had some significant content cuts or rushed/unrefined areas due to pressure from the publisher to release by a specific date.

Hell, one game I worked on needed about 2-3 more months to get it polished and ready, but the publisher was so hell bent on the release date that they considered cutting the entire game and only releasing what was the bonus unlockable content - 4 open source SHMUP flash games we ported to the Wii - for the same price. We worked 12 hour days 7 days/week for a few months to prevent that from happening. The last half of the campaign still shipped very unpolished, but it at least had a decent community following for content creation.
